subject: Post-call: Region corridor & residency constraints for NobleBank — deployment options
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Mullen <sarah.mullen@noblebank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-09T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Region corridor & residency constraints for NobleBank — deployment options

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + items we need to unblock the architecture recommendation for the pilot:

Summary of constraints you called out:
- Pilot: EU-only (Frankfurt) for any production-like traffic; sandbox/dev can remain on hosted in us-east for internal testing.
- Production: eventual requirement for Private VPC or Dedicated capacity in both EU (Frankfurt) and APAC (Tokyo) for payment and PII flows.
- Cross-region read access: some analytics will come from APAC systems; acceptable if routing through a controlled proxy, but data-at-rest must stay in-region.

Questions to help us size options (short answers are fine):
1) Expected steady-state throughput for pilot (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and peak concurrency.
2) Scope of data residency for pilot vs full prod (only payment transactions? telemetry allowed out-of-region?).
3) Procurement timeline and whether a standard SOW is required before pilot kickoff.

Next steps we propose:
- We'll draft a short 2-page comparison: Hosted EU-only (EU region) vs Dedicated reserved capacity (EU) vs Private VPC (EU + APAC). That will include latency, estimated monthly cost range, and minimum SLA differences.
- Technical deep-dive with your infra/security team (30–45 min) — can you share preferred windows?
- I'll attach a first-pass MAP (mutual action plan) and a blank procurement checklist for your team to annotate.

Attachments: Mutual action plan (draft), procurement checklist (stub) — see attachments referenced below.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (docx), procurement-checklist-template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sarah Mullen <sarah.mullen@noblebank.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Admin <itadmin@noblebank.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@noblebank.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T11:02:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Region corridor & residency constraints for NobleBank — deployment options

Hi Avery — thanks for the summary. Confirming the points from the call and adding a few clarifications:

- Pilot requirements: EU-only (AWS eu-central-1 / Frankfurt). Pilot will process anonymized transaction metadata but must be provably resident in EU. No cross-region backups for pilot.
- Prod requirements: Payment workflows must be in-region and behind our VPC/VPN. We are evaluating Dedicated vs Private VPC; security prefers Private VPC for long-term but procurement will weigh cost.
- APAC scope: Our Singapore/Tokyo teams need read-only access for aggregated analytics; we require data transfer to be via an approved WAN link (we can share network peering requirements).

Answers to your questions:
1) Pilot traffic estimate: ~30 rps steady, burst to 150 rps during peak business hours. Token load likely modest (short prompts) — estimate ~150k tokens/day.
2) Data residency scope: For pilot, only non-identifiable transaction metadata may be processed; payment payloads must be stubbed. For prod, full payment payloads must never leave respective region.
3) Procurement timeline: We can start the pilot contract in Feb — procurement prefers a short pilot SOW (30–60 days) and then a separate production SOW.

I've attached the security roster and pointed IT to coordinate the deep-dive. Available times for infra call next week: Tue 2027-01-12 09:00–11:00 CET or Wed 2027-01-13 13:00–15:00 CET.

Best,
Sarah Mullen
Sr. Product Manager, NobleBank

Attachment: NobleBank_Security_Roster.xlsx (xlsx)
